content.title: Regression Predictions and Residuals
content.overview: This lesson focuses on using a linear regression equation to predict outcomes and calculating the residual to measure the accuracy of those predictions. You will learn to determine if a data point falls above or below the regression line based on the sign of the residual.
learning_objectives: Calculate a predicted y-value (ŷ) using a given regression equation and an x-value.
Compute the residual for a specific data point using the formula: Residual = Actual y − Predicted y.
Interpret the sign and magnitude of a residual in the context of the data.

sections.title: The Regression Equation and Prediction
sections.content: A regression line, often written as ŷ = mx + b or ŷ = a + bx, is a mathematical model used to predict the value of a dependent variable (y) based on an independent variable (x). The symbol ŷ (read as 'y-hat') represents the predicted value. To find a prediction, simply substitute the given x-value into the equation and solve for ŷ.

sections.title: Calculating Residuals
sections.content: A residual is the vertical distance between an observed data point (Actual y) and the regression line (Predicted y). It represents the 'error' of the model for that specific point. The formula is: Residual = y - ŷ. It is critical to subtract the predicted value from the actual value, not the other way around.

sections.title: Interpreting the Residual
sections.content:
The sign of the residual tells you the position of the actual data point relative to the regression line. A positive residual means the actual value is higher than the predicted value (the point is above the line). A negative residual means the actual value is lower than the predicted value (the point is below the line). A residual of zero means the actual data point lies exactly on the regression line.

![A scatter plot showing a regression line with one point above the line (positive residual) and one point below the line (negative residual).](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/615edd53-0516-4076-8804-c277e6dd8dfb-1786506193911-26.webp)

worked_examples.question: A researcher uses the regression line ŷ = 10 + 5x to model the relationship between years of experience (x) and hourly wage (y). An employee with 4 years of experience earns $32 per hour. Calculate the residual and interpret its meaning.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Identify the actual y-value. The employee earns $32, so y = 32. Step 2: Calculate the predicted value (ŷ) by plugging x = 4 into the equation: ŷ = 10 + 5(4) = 10 + 20 = 30. Step 3: Calculate the residual using the formula Residual = y - ŷ. Residual = 32 - 30 = 2. Step 4: Interpret the result. The residual is 2, meaning the employee earns $2 more per hour than the model predicted.

common_mistakes: Reversing the residual formula (calculating Predicted - Actual instead of Actual - Predicted).
Confusing the predicted value (ŷ) with the actual value (y) given in the problem.
Misinterpreting a negative residual as 'better' or 'higher' when it actually indicates the observed value is below the prediction.
exam_tips: Always calculate the predicted value (ŷ) first before attempting to find the residual.
Remember the phrase 'Actual minus Predicted' (A - P) to keep the subtraction order correct.
If a point is above the line on a scatterplot, its residual must be positive.
content.recap: To analyze bivariate data using regression, use the equation to find the predicted ŷ. The residual (y - ŷ) measures the prediction error; positive residuals indicate the model underestimated the value, while negative residuals indicate an overestimate.

knowledge_claims.content: The variable ŷ (y-hat) represents the predicted value of the dependent variable in a regression equation.
To find a predicted value, substitute the given x-value into the regression equation and solve for ŷ.
The formula for a residual is Residual = Actual y − Predicted ŷ.
A positive residual indicates that the actual observed value is greater than the value predicted by the regression line.
A negative residual indicates that the actual observed value is less than the value predicted by the regression line.
On a scatterplot, a data point located above the regression line has a positive residual.
On a scatterplot, a data point located below the regression line has a negative residual.
Calculating the residual as Predicted minus Actual is a common error that flips the sign of the result.
A residual measures the vertical distance between an observed data point and the regression line.
If the actual value equals the predicted value, the residual is exactly zero.
The magnitude (absolute value) of a residual represents the size of the prediction error in the units of the y-variable.
If a regression model overestimates a value, the resulting residual for that data point will be negative.
